protocol.title: Microfluidic Chip Fabrication (full pipeline)
protocol.summary: End-to-end PDMS microfluidic chip fab: SLA mold print + cure → PDMS mixing + degassing → soft lithography → plasma bond to coverslip.

meta.authors_note: Original authors: Ethan Lin, Alia Starman. Last update: 2026-05-06.

attrs.label: PDMS crosslinker volume
attrs.description: Standard 10:1 monomer:crosslinker mix. Adjust monomer volume to scale; ratio defaults to 10:1 (Sylgard 184 standard).

children.body: Default values produce a typical [!var:pdms_total_mL] batch from [!var:monomer_vol_mL] of monomer + [!var:crosslinker_vol_mL] of crosslinker. Scale the monomer volume to your chip count.

sections.label: Mold making — Resin (~20 min active, ≥1 day until usable)

children.body: Check the resin level to ensure there is enough, and clean the resin plate with a scraper.
Put the resin plate into the printer, lock in place, and close the lid. Push open the chimney (air outlet) of the resin cart.
Upload the .stl file of your print into PreForm. Confirm settings match the resin type (usually BioMed Clear).

Orient the part correctly for the intended use. SLA prints layer-by-layer, so for absolutely flat features, keep them parallel to the base plate. Supports are often used for complex shapes and make removal easier — but a chamfer bottom can avoid the need for supports altogether.
Start printing. Once the print is uploaded, the USB can be unhooked from the printer.
When the print is finished, take the plate out and scrape down uncured resin around the parts back into the printer.

Remove the parts from the mounting plate using the scraper. Spray with IPA to initially clear off uncured resin. If you didn't use supports, slide the scraper between the part and the metal plate (plate facing down) and lever the part off carefully.
Put the parts into the IPA cleaner for 20–30 min. (In the McGhee lab, you may need to move the round plug adapter from the curing chamber over to the cleaner.)
Add the parts to the Draft V2 resin bath for 1 hour (do NOT leave for much longer). Spray with IPA after this secondary wash.
UV cure for 1 hour at 60 C. (Move the round plug adapter from the IPA bath to the UV curing chamber.)
Put the cured mold in an 80 C oven overnight before pouring the first PDMS chip.

Uncured resin is a skin sensitizer — wear gloves throughout the print pickup, IPA wash, and resin-bath steps. Do not skip the 80 C overnight bake before first PDMS pour, or the chip surface will be tacky.
By volume in the McGhee lab to reduce mess and avoid contaminating the scale. Monomer + crosslinker aliquots are stored in syringe tubes for repeated use.
For the crosslinker aliquot: remove the plunger of a 10 mL syringe tube. Put a 3D-printed cap on, and pour 8–9 mL of crosslinker in through the top, then re-insert the plunger.
For the monomer aliquot: open the bucket and fill 25 mL syringe tubes. Only dip the protrusion of the tube into the liquid — keep the body clean.
Mix a batch: in a large weight boat, add 10:1 monomer:crosslinker. Default = [!var:monomer_vol_mL] monomer → [!var:crosslinker_vol_mL] crosslinker. Add the monomer FIRST, then the crosslinker.
Keep full control of the crosslinker syringe when dispensing — it can spray out under pressure. Always add monomer to the boat first; adding crosslinker first risks splash.
With a wooden stick, mix vigorously for ~3 minutes. The mix should turn white from the air bubbles you're introducing — the white-out tells you it's homogeneously mixed.

Once mixed, pour from the top into a new 25 mL syringe: pull the plunger out of the body, fit the 3D-printed cap onto the syringe opening to prevent leak, pour the PDMS through the top, then put the plunger back in and push it until it clicks. Flip the syringe over and wait for the air bubble to migrate up.

Label the new aliquot "10:1 PDMS" with a date and your initials. Put it into the -20 C PDMS bucket, cap-side down. After a few hours of cold storage the bubbles will have settled and the aliquot is usable.

If you need PDMS immediately with no aliquots: after mixing, put the weight boat into a vacuum (lay down paper towels — it can overflow). Turn on the vacuum until air bubbles stop forming, then proceed to soft lithography.

sections.label: Chip making — Soft lithography (15 min active, 1 hr wait)

children.body: Push the desired amount of 10:1 PDMS into the mold. Don't pour over the inlet/outlet holes — that creates a sealed bubble pocket.

Place the mold into a plastic tray and into the vacuum chamber to remove any bubbles introduced during pouring. Turn on the vacuum. Don't fill the chip fully if using vacuum — it will bubble over (the plastic tray catches the overflow). Any remaining big bubbles can be fished out with a pipette tip.
Put the degassed mold into an 80 C oven for at least 1 hour to cure fully.

sections.label: Chip making — Plasma bonding (20 min active, 1 hr wait)

children.body: Clean off the glass coverslip with IPA, a lens-cleaner cloth, and tape. Use compressed air if necessary.

Remove the PDMS from the mold: spray IPA on top, insert the thin, rounded point of the spatula between the mold and the PDMS, and lever it free. Try to remove parallel to the channel direction and lift slowly — cured correctly, the PDMS should maintain its features.
Clean the PDMS surface with tape and compressed air.
Place the glass coverslip and PDMS into the plasma chamber. Make sure the CHANNEL-SIDE of the PDMS is face up.

Set up the plasma chamber: turn the barometer and plasma chamber on. Turn the BLACK knob on the plasma chamber all the way to the right to open the vacuum line. Switch the vacuum on (you'll hear it start up) and slightly press the door to the chamber to create the seal. Wait until vacuum reads ~1 torr.

Turn on the desired gas tanks by twisting their main silver knobs. Twist the SILVER knob near the black plasma-chamber knob open — flowmeter bubbles will bob up slightly. Use the flowmeter knobs to get O₂ ≈ 10 and Ar ≈ 1. Pressure will rise again; wait until it decreases back to ~1 torr.
Turn on plasma to HIGH for 1 minute. You should see a white haze inside the chamber (see appendix figure).
Reverse the setup: turn plasma off, shut the silver knob, turn off the gas tanks, shut the vacuum off. Slowly let air back into the chamber by twisting the black knob.

Take out the PDMS and the glass slide slowly without touching the surfaces facing up. Put the PDMS channel-side onto the coverslip. You'll see the opacity change from cloudy to clear/darker where plasma bonding has happened.

DO NOT press hard on the bonded surface. Only if absolutely necessary, use a spatula and press lightly around the edges to initiate bonding contact. Pressing on the channels collapses the features and ruins the chip.
Place the chip into the 80 C oven for at least 30 minutes to finish bonding.
If you want inlet/outlet tubes with PDMS, add them now and let cure for another 1 hour before use.
General schematic of a microfluidic chip: glass coverslip on bottom, PDMS chip on top with channel features, inlet/outlet pipette tips inserted into through-holes.

children.body: Pipette depth: the pipette tip does not reach the bottom of the chip, leaving space for flow to happen between the tip's end and the channel floor.

children.body: Plasma treatment set-up with labeled controls: 4a) vacuum + plasma on/off + barometer on/off, 4b) black knob (vacuum line), 4e) silver knob (gas line), 4f) flowmeter knobs (O₂ + Ar), 4g) plasma level dial.

attrs.image_alt: Plasma treatment chamber with labeled controls for vacuum, gas flow, and plasma level

children.body: Typical gas-cylinder set-up. 4d) Main gas tank knob is the one you twist open for plasma treatment. The cylinder pressure gauge shows tank fill (low → reorder); the delivery pressure gauge shows what's actually being sent to the plasma chamber — keep this low. The regulator dial sets the delivery pressure.

attrs.image_alt: Gas cylinder regulator with labeled main tank knob, delivery pressure gauge, cylinder pressure gauge, regulator dial

children.body: Plasma haze visible through the chamber window — confirms the plasma is on.

attrs.image_alt: Glowing plasma haze through the plasma chamber window

children.body: If the delivery-pressure gauge isn't shooting up after opening the main gas tank knob, the tank is likely empty. Order replacement gas tanks as soon as you see them running low — long lead times.
